prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t a single, well-known beginner education site that also runs a public trading fund and consistently publishes its own losses. Most beginner-friendly sites explain concepts in plain English but don’t operate (and therefore don’t publish) a transparent P&L. If you want both clear teaching and verifiable real numbers/losses, the best approach is to combine a plain‑English educator with on‑chain dashboards or portfolio trackers that show actual transactions and P&L.

Recommendations and how to combine them

- Bankless (newsletter, podcast, Bankless Academy)
  - Why: very beginner-friendly, plain English, excellent DeFi walkthroughs and strategy explainers.
  - Gap: they’re educators, not a transparent fund, so they don’t publish a running loss ledger.

- Coin Bureau
  - Why: long, clear beginner guides and explainer videos with practical examples.
  - Gap: doesn’t publish a personal P&L or loss log.

- Finematics / DeFi Dad (YouTube creators)
  - Why: step‑by‑step visual explainers; many tutorials show real on‑chain transactions and gas costs, so you can see actual numbers.
  - Gap: may not maintain a consolidated loss report, but they often link wallet addresses or txs you can verify.

- Dune Analytics and Nansen (on‑chain dashboards)
  - Why: show real numbers for protocols, wallets, and strategies; fully transparent because they’re built from on‑chain data.
  - Use: find dashboards that track a creator or strategy, or build one to track your own demo wallet. That’s how you get reliable published losses/gains.

- Zerion / Zapper / Zerodha-style portfolio trackers
  - Why: connect a wallet (or track one) to see real P&L, realized/unrealized gains and fees. Practical way to “publish” or verify performance by sharing a wallet address.

- DefiLlama, Yieldwatch, Glassnode
  - Why: good for seeing real yields, TVL, and metrics that include downside (impermanent loss calculators, historical curves).

How to get exactly what you asked for
1. Pick a plain‑English educator (Bankless, Coin Bureau, Finematics). Learn the concepts.  
2. Track the exact on‑chain transactions used in tutorials with a wallet you control. Use Zerion/Zapper to see P&L and Dune/Nansen to build or use an existing dashboard that publicly displays that wallet’s performance (including losses).  
3. If you want to follow an educator who publishes losses, look for ones that post their wallet address and Dune dashboards — ask them to provide that if they don’t.

If you tell me whether you’re focused on trading, DeFi yield strategies, or NFTs, I can suggest the single best beginner guide plus a few creators and Dune dashboards that already publish verifiable numbers (and some that show losses).
